The feeder number is a location identifier that identifies a specific power distribution area. In the DPV ontology, Location is classified as PersonalData and Tracking. A feeder number can be cross-referenced with public grid maps to identify a specific geographic area where residents live, enabling indirect identification of individuals in that area. Under GDPR, location data that can identify a person's residence area is considered personal data.

The substation number is a location identifier that identifies a specific electrical substation and its service area. Similar to feeder, it can be used to identify a specific geographic region. In the DPV ontology, Location is a type of PersonalData and Tracking. Combined with feeder, it narrows down the exact area, increasing re-identification risk for residents and businesses in that zone.

The date column represents measurement timestamps for grid data. While dates can be part of personal data when linked to an individual (e.g., LifeHistory), in this context they are temporal markers for aggregate infrastructure measurements. They do not directly identify any individual and are necessary for time-series analysis of grid performance.

This is an aggregate count of housing units (70-72) in the feeder area. While the DPV ontology defines Household as PersonalData related to 'personal or household activities', a count of 70+ units is sufficiently aggregated to prevent identification of specific households. The value is statistical and does not reveal information about any individual household.

This is an aggregate count of industry and commerce units (11) in the area. While it relates to professional/commercial entities, the count is a statistical aggregate that does not identify specific businesses or individuals. The number 11 is large enough to prevent re-identification of individual commercial entities.
